Let \(x\) be the mass of NaHCO₃ and \(y\) be the mass of MgCO₃.

\[
x+y=15.00
\]

Residue from NaHCO₃:
\[
2\text{NaHCO}_3 \rightarrow \text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3
\]
Molar mass NaHCO₃ = 84.006 g/mol, Na₂CO₃ = 105.988 g/mol  
Residue factor:
\[
\frac{105.988}{2(84.006)} = 0.630836
\]

Residue from MgCO₃:
\[
\text{MgCO}_3 \rightarrow \text{MgO}
\]
Molar mass MgCO₃ = 84.313 g/mol, MgO = 40.304 g/mol  
Residue factor:
\[
\frac{40.304}{84.313} = 0.478028
\]

So:
\[
0.630836x + 0.478028(15-x)=8.80
\]
\[
0.152808x = 1.629575
\]
\[
x = 10.664 \text{ g}
\]

Mass percentage of NaHCO₃:
\[
\frac{10.664}{15.00}\times 100 = 71.1\%
\]

ANSWER: 71.1
